It's too soon!' but Arthur pushes through the door into the bedroom, following the tubes to where they connect to Saito's wrist. He speaks softly, recalling a man he once met in a distant, dreamlike encounter—a man known for radical ideas. The top continues to spin, steady and graceful, as the camera holds on its rotating form.

name: Cobb Confronts Saito in the Hidden Apartment
description: Cobb sits with Saito's gun turning in his hand while Nash holds Saito's arms behind his back. Outside, the sounds of rioting grow louder. Cobb remarks that Saito came prepared, pointing to the gun. Saito demands to know how Cobb found the apartment, insisting that even his head of security doesn't know about it. Cobb responds that it's hard for a man in Saito's position to keep a secret place entirely hidden, especially when a married woman is involved. Saito denies that she would have revealed it, but Cobb remains firm. He tells Saito they don't have everything they came for—the key piece of information wasn't there. Arthur, standing at the window, turns and says the crowd is getting closer.

name: The Dream Begins to Unravel

The rhythm of the sound matches the slow tick of Arthur's watch, each second marked with increasing weight. Shouts rise up the stairs, overlapping with the swelling noise. Arthur glances at his watch, his expression steady but focused. The carpet beneath Saito shifts under his cheek as Cobb presses him down, the gun firm against his face. Saito's eyes move to the floor, then he begins to laugh, murmuring about the carpet—how it’s wrong, not wool but polyester.

As the distant, low horns grow louder and the shouts from the stairs rise, Saito begins to laugh. He remarks on the carpet beneath him, noting it is polyester, not wool, and says he has always hated the original one for being stained and frayed.

name: Saito Notices the Carpet and Realizes It's a Dream
description: Saito lies on the floor, the gun pressed to his cheek, when he notices the carpet beneath him. He comments on how he's always hated it—stained, frayed, and supposedly wool. Then he corrects himself: it's polyester. He begins to laugh, scornful and certain. Cobb glances down at the carpet, then up at Nash, who shrugs, unsure. Saito's laughter lingers, filled with the quiet triumph of realization.

name: Cobb Disrupts Saito's Authority in the Dream
description: Saito approached Cobb with confidence, speaking as if the dream were under his control. As Nash stood behind him, Saito declared that they should play by his rules. Before he could finish, Cobb interrupted, stating they were not in Saito's dream. Saito turned toward Cobb, but Cobb had already vanished. Saito spun around to face Nash, only to find Nash gone as well. At that moment, the door burst open, torn from its hinges by a surge of rioters who flooded into the room. The space fell silent, the light dimming as the figures stood motionless amidst the wreckage.

Cobb vanishes from the room

name: Nash Claims the Dream and Vanishes

The moment the words leave his mouth, the door explodes inward as rioters surge into the room, rushing toward him. But Nash is no longer there. The rioters fill the space, swarming over where he stood, only to find him gone. The room falls silent, the light fading as Saito remains, surrounded by the chaos that has overtaken the space.
related_events: Nash reveals the dream is his own
Nash disappears before the rioters
Rioters break through the door and swarm the room

name: The Room Falls Silent

description: A low tremor rumbles through the castle. Cobb and Arthur steady themselves against the wooden rail as tiles and pieces of masonry fall from the structure into the churning black sea below. Guests wander the massive terraces, unaware or unfazed. Arthur and Cobb exchange words about the mission. Cobb states that he can get the information—they know it's in the safe, having seen the target's reaction when secrets were mentioned. Arthur nods, then notices someone approaching. He brushes past Mal, shaking his head, and tells Cobb to handle things. Cobb tells Arthur to go to his room, assuring him he will take care of the rest.

Cobb identifies location of critical information in a safe

name: Arthur Confronts Cobb About Mal's Presence
description: Arthur sees Mal standing on the terrace and turns to Cobb, asking why she is there. Cobb responds that he will handle it. Without another word to him, Arthur walks past Mal, brushing close as he leaves, his expression stern and disapproving.

Arthur brushes past Mal while expressing disapproval

name: Mal Confronts Cobb on the Terrace
description: A low tremor rumbles through the castle. Cobb and Arthur steady themselves against the wooden rail as tiles and masonry fall into the churning black sea below. Guests wander the terraces. Arthur sees Mal and asks Cobb what she is doing here. Cobb tells Arthur to go to his room and leave the rest to him. Arthur brushes past Mal, shaking his head. Mal approaches Cobb and looks out over the edge, the wind whipping her hair. She asks if she would survive a jump into the sea. Cobb says perhaps, with a clean dive. He asks why she is here. She turns to him, amused, and says she thought he might be missing her. He leans in, mesmerized, and admits he does. But he adds that he can no longer trust her. She stares up at him, inviting, and says, 'So what?'

name: Cobb and Arthur Pitch Dream Extraction to Saito
description: Cobb and Arthur sit with Saito at a lavish table, where Cobb gestures to the meal and asks if the threat is a bacteria, a virus, or an intestinal worm. Saito pauses, fork in mid-air, as Cobb grins and corrects himself—it's an idea. He explains that once an idea takes hold in the brain, it is nearly impossible to remove, no matter how hard someone tries to ignore it. Saito questions whether such a thing could truly be forgotten, and Cobb insists that while information can be lost, a fully formed idea lingers deep in the mind. Saito wonders if such an idea could be stolen. Arthur steps in, clarifying that in the dream state, a person's conscious defenses weaken, making their thoughts vulnerable to theft—a process called extraction. Cobb adds that he can train Saito's subconscious to defend itself, because he is the most skilled extractor, familiar with every method of infiltration. Leaning forward, Cobb tells Saito that for the training to work, he must be completely open, allowing Cobb to know his thoughts better than anyone else. He gestures around the room, asking if Saito has a safe full of secrets in his dreams—Cobb needs to know what is inside. Saito offers a faint smile, rises, and departs through double doors that open onto a grand party, leaving the two men behind. Arthur turns to Cobb, concerned, but Cobb silences him. A tremor runs through the room, glasses tremble, and Cobb glances at his watch—the second hand is frozen.

Arthur clarifies Cobb's metaphor about mental theft
Cobb offers to train Saito's subconscious to resist extraction

As the doors close behind him, Arthur turns to Cobb, his voice low with worry, suggesting that Saito may have seen through their pitch. Cobb raises a finger to his lips, signaling silence. At that moment, a tremor ripples through the room. The glasses on the table tremble, and Cobb glances at his watch—the second hand has stopped moving, frozen in place.

Nash checks Cobb’s wrist, where two yellow tubes are taped above his watch. The second hand on the watch moves unnaturally slow. Outside, rioters fill the streets of a chaotic city, smashing and burning. Nash moves to the window, peers through the parted curtains, then turns back to the silver briefcase at Arthur’s feet. Tubes run from the case to Arthur’s wrist, and another set disappears under the door to the bedroom, where Saito lies asleep on a bed, also connected by tubes to his wrist. A sudden explosion booms nearby, shaking the room, and Nash reacts as the tension in the air sharpens.

name: Cobb Questions Nash's Fate and Saito Proposes Inception
description: The helicopter rises into the air as Saito gestures for Cobb and Arthur to sit. Nash is pulled from the chopper by Saito's bodyguards and dragged across the landing pad. Cobb watches the scene in silence, then turns to Saito. 'What will you do to him?' he asks. Saito replies that he won't do anything, but cannot guarantee Nash's safety from Cobol Engineering. As the city glides beneath them, Cobb asks what Saito wants. Saito responds with a single word: 'Inception.' Arthur raises his eyebrows, skeptical, and argues that planting an idea is impossible because the mind always recognizes its origin. Saito counters that the idea could be planted subconsciously. Cobb remains quiet, then says it is possible. When Saito asks if he can do it, Cobb refuses. Saito offers the stolen information as payment. Cobb asks if he is being given a choice. Saito says he is. Cobb chooses to leave.

name: Saito Proposes Inception
description: Saito asks Cobb and Arthur if it's possible to plant an idea in someone's mind. Arthur responds by telling Saito, "Don't think about elephants." Saito admits he is thinking about elephants. Arthur explains that the idea only exists because he planted it, and the subject always knows it came from elsewhere. Saito suggests the idea could be planted subconsciously. Arthur replies that a person can always trace the origin of an idea, and that real inspiration cannot be faked. Cobb then says it is possible to plant an idea. Saito asks Cobb if he can do it. Cobb says he won't. Saito offers the information Cobb was paid to steal in exchange. Cobb asks if he is being given a choice. Saito says he is. Cobb says he chooses to leave.

name: Cobb's Phone Call with His Children
description: The phone rings, and Cobb answers, hearing the voices of his children. He greets them, and they respond quietly. He asks who said they were just okay, and his son James confirms it’s him. James asks when Cobb is coming home. Cobb tells him he can’t return yet, explaining again that he’s working. His daughter Philippa says their grandmother believes he will never come back. Cobb pauses, then asks to speak with her. Philippa says Grandma is shaking her head. Cobb tenses, gripping the phone tightly. He tells them they’ll have to hope Grandma is wrong. James asks if their mother is with him. Cobb flinches, then says no, that Mommy is gone. James asks where she is, but before Cobb can answer, their grandmother calls them away, telling them it’s time to go. Cobb quickly says he’ll send presents through Grandpa and to be good. The line goes dead. Cobb stares at the phone, then downs his drink.
